queue.title: Ascending vacuum tubes: cross-floor continuity + a player ±1-floor hop
queue.resolution: Shipped 2026-05-31 in two commits. (1) shared/vacuum_tube.gd renders one-story corner segments built per-floor (floors 1/3/4 + Garden via iso_tubes), tiling corner-to-corner up the stack like the spine pipes; top floor seals its caps. (2) shared/vacuum_lift.gd (top-level, mirrors elevator_platform): grounded-in-a-mouth jump = quick suction hop UP one floor, hold-down = DOWN one floor (a third vertical-traversal method, served floors 1-4 so it also reaches the Canopy); plus produce-tinted item-transit capsules rising through the current floor's tube. Slab-safe arrival via GameState.tube_hopping tracked in tower_controller's _current_level gate (same fix class as F-022); verified 2->3 lands on the Floor 3 slab and stays (no fall-through), 3->2 returns clean. Did NOT fold in Q-004: the tubes sit at the four CORNERS, independent of the central elevator-shaft hole, so the open-shaft decision is still its own thing. Tube body translucency reads subtly from the top-down iso angle (collars+glow mark each mouth clearly) — candidate for an aesthetic pass if the operator wants the columns more present.
queue.detail: Operator's next pickup. Evolve the four CORNER vacuum tubes (scenes/floor_2/iso_tubes.gd — one per corner, currently Garden-only sell-down-for-cash) into ASCENDING tubes that run continuously UP THROUGH every floor, tiling corner-to-corner the way the elevator spine pipes now do (one story tall per floor, see FLOOR_1_SPINE_PIPE_*). Two jobs: (1) OBJECTS pass through them between floors (produce/cargo travel up as well as down — the cross-floor item conduit the tube comments already gesture at), creating visible continuity through the stack; (2) the PLAYER can jump THROUGH a tube to travel up or down a SINGLE floor — a vacuum-lift hop, distinct from the elevator (multi-floor ride) and the stairs (3<->4). So tubes become a third vertical-traversal method, scoped to ±1 floor. Build on the stacked-tower offset-safety patterns (Y-gate + local-frame). Reuse the slab-layer gating insight: a tube hop needs the destination floor solid on arrival (see the elevator-ride current_level fix, F-022-era / commit 79021ff). Note the four corner tubes already exist on every floor via iso_tubes; this is about making them span + be traversable. NOT started — operator explicitly deferred.

queue.title: Garden (Floor 2) economy — dissect the full service + where it leads
queue.detail: Operator wants to hold this thought for a future session (timing TBD). The Garden currently runs TWO quantities: backpack_count (items carried, cap BACKPACK_CAPACITY=20, +1 per harvest — consistent) and food_count (sum of each crop's VALUE: tomato 1, pumpkin 1, pepper 2, cucumber 3, blueberries 5, eggplant 15). Selling at a corner vacuum tube converts food_count * TUBE_SELL_VALUE_MULTIPLIER -> cash and zeroes both backpack_count and food_count (iso_tubes._sell_at). Harvest floaters were just made consistent (every crop shows '+1 <Crop>', uniform green — commit fc0e935) BUT food_count += value still happens under the hood, so the value economy is invisible right now. Open questions for the design session: is 'value' meant to be per-crop worth or just item count? Should the two currencies merge? The tubes 'send produce down to Floor 1 and out into the world for cash' (iso_tubes header) — the Garden -> Utility -> economy pipeline is stubbed but not wired to anything real yet (no diner/population consumer). Decide what the Garden's full service produces and what consumes it before re-surfacing per-crop value in the UI. NOTE: 'Garden' = Floor 2 (the original brief's stale 'Floor 3' label refers to the Garden; canonical Floor 3 is the Arboretum).

queue.title: Open elevator shaft hole — fall-through-by-design decision
queue.resolution: Resolved Session 9 (operator hit it: tube-hop to a floor, walk into the elevator, fall down the open shaft to the car/bottom). Fix: an INVISIBLE collision 'shaft grate' across the opening on every floor with a hole (FloorChrome.build_slab shaft branch covers garden/arboretum_ground/residential/sky_lounge/roof; arboretum_canopy adds its own to the tiled slab). Collision-only (no mesh) so it never blocks the view of the cabin; it's a child of SlabBody so the tower gates it per-floor exactly like the slab (off for floors above -> jumps still pass up; a ride owns the transform so it passes too). The player now stands at the shaft and calls/rides instead of falling. Verified with _shaft_harness.tscn (player HELD at floor level over the shaft, no fall).
queue.detail: The slab on every served floor (now 1/2/4/5, 0-indexed) has a central ~4x4 hole for the elevator car to travel through. When the car is parked on another floor, walking into that hole drops the player down the open shaft. The jump/elevator fall-through bugs were fixed (commit 79021ff), but this open-shaft drop is geometry-by-design and may be the 'fall through in some instances' the operator still felt. Decide the intended behaviour: auto-call the car when the player nears the empty shaft, a retractable safety grate, leave it as an intentional hazard, or fold it into the Q-002 tube-hop traversal. NOTE: the two new blank floors (Residential 4, Sky Lounge 5) also have this central shaft hole, so whatever's decided applies tower-wide.

queue.title: Fifth autoload (GameDirector) — relax the four-autoloads convention
queue.resolution: Greenlit by Jared (narrative-arc handoff D.1; the 'four autoloads only' line was a convention, never code-enforced). Session 10 step 1: GameDirector registered as the 5th autoload in project.godot, AFTER AudioManager (Constants, GameState, SaveManager, AudioManager, GameDirector). It is the phase/state sequencer for the 7-step arc — owns the Phase enum + current_phase + phase_changed signal; reads and MIRRORS GameState (GameState.phase), never holds a parallel copy. Litmus: 'what is true in the world' -> GameState; 'what should happen next and when' -> GameDirector.
queue.detail: Was open decision D.1 in the handoff. Logged resolved for the record; no further action.

queue.title: Exterior opening is IN-WORLD inside tower.tscn (no scene swap)
queue.resolution: Locked by Jared (Session-9 follow-up; handoff D.3). The new EMPTY_LOT / HIRE_PARTNER opening beats are spaces INSIDE the existing tower.tscn — NO change_scene_to_file, NO separate intro scene. run/main_scene stays res://scenes/tower/tower.tscn. A boot flag in constants.gd selects the START STATE within the same scene (real opening -> EMPTY_LOT + exterior spawn; dev fallback -> straight to today's Garden spawn); it does NOT point at a different scene. 'Entering the tower' = the player traverses in / the camera moves to Floor 0, never a load. Because it's one scene, tower_hud.gd persists so the per-phase objective line works across the exterior beats with no second HUD. Honors the one-continuous-world architecture (rules/stacked_tower_invariants.md).
queue.detail: Was open decision D.3 (exterior shape) in the handoff — resolved to the in-world option. Implemented incrementally in steps 2-3 of this phase; the boot flag + exterior land in step 2.

queue.title: Floor-population first increment = thinner 'life layer' on the existing grid (not a full reframe)
queue.resolution: Took the floor_population_spec's own recommendation (the load-bearing sub-decision flagged 'don't guess blind in-engine'). The Garden's auto-built plot grid + dispenser STAY; placement adds a thinner life layer on top. Concretely: all 30x30 plots boot DORMANT (bare ground, not plantable); placing a planter bed activates a 3x3 ZONE of the existing grid (dormant -> tilled/plantable). Proves the placement->alive loop without gutting the crop economy or the dispenser wiring. Promote to the full player-placed-grid reframe once the loop feels right. Threshold: GARDEN_ALIVE_BED_COUNT=3 beds -> ALIVE. Chain is now enter(barren) -> Cody power_utilities -> power 6 sources -> gate lifts to PLACEMENT (Cody 'let's build it out, drop your first planter bed') -> place 3 beds -> Garden crosses ALIVE (provisional bloom: grow-lights warm in) -> Cody 'go ahead and plant' -> planting unlocks. interiors_unlocked now gates PLACEMENT; new GameState.garden.alive gates PLANTING.

queue.title: Construction dollhouse reads as 'the game froze' — clarity/UX pass
queue.resolution: Shipped Session 14 (4 commits, screenshot-verified). Operator reframed it: B DID work (you keep pressing it), the real gaps were (a) no on-screen 'press B' cue, (b) wrong viewpoint — the player wanted to STAND BACK as a visible builder and watch each floor rise, (c) doors out were on the basement but you entered the Garden, and (d) the 'basement' showing at the start. Fixes: (1) RE-ANCHOR (Constants.GROUND_LEVEL=1) — the Garden is now the at-grade ground floor (world y=0), Utility basement drops below grade (y=-6, hidden under the site ground); world-Y is (level-GROUND_LEVEL)*story everywhere (tower offset + elevator + vacuum lift + fall-backstop), so site ground / empty lot / Garden share y=0 with no hacks. (2) DOOR CONTINUITY — doorways moved from the basement to the Garden (iso_floor._build_one_wall gained a `doored` split mirroring FloorChrome; utility back to solid); walk in at grade -> the Garden, no vertical teleport. (3) BUILDER'S-EYE CONSTRUCTION — the builder is VISIBLE standing back on the site (CONSTRUCT_VIEW_BACK) facing the build, frozen until top-out; grounded exterior framing centred on the tower, widening as it grows; collapsed the dollhouse->ground ease (builder already on the ground). (4) BIG CENTRAL PROMPT — 'PRESS B TO RAISE YOUR TOWER / Floor N of 6' translucent banner low on screen with a scale-punch confirm per floor, 'STEP INSIDE' on top-out; hidden in interior play. (5) HID the dead CameraModesHud during construction + exterior walk. (6) RESIZE HARDENING — _aspect_fit grows the ortho size below 16:9 so a narrow/portrait window never clips the tower (live, smooth). Verified: traversal lands solid (vacuum + elevator), build->walk-in unregressed, narrow-window framing fits. Commits bdcd8f5, 642e41c, 3720414, 11315ea.
queue.detail: Playtest (Session 13): after hiring the partner, the player drops into the external dollhouse BUILD_STRUCTURE view ('FLOOR 0 OF 6'; press B six times to raise the tower, then the camera eases down to a walkable character to explore + walk in). It WORKS AS DESIGNED but reads as broken/stuck because: (1) the player is hidden + frozen by design, (2) the ISO/PROFILE/OVER-SHOULDER camera buttons (CameraModesHud) are still visible but DEAD (iso_camera bows out during construction + exterior walk), (3) the only affordance is a tiny corner '[B] raise the next floor' prompt that's easy to miss. Operator also reported the view is 'glitchy when resizing the window' (likely the dollhouse orthographic framing reflowing on aspect-ratio change) and asked 'is the game unstable?' — it is NOT, this is purely a clarity problem. FIXES: (1) a big central 'Press B to raise your tower — Floor N of 6' prompt with a confirm beat on each build; (2) hide CameraModesHud during construction AND the exterior walk (they do nothing then); (3) harden the camera against window resize. OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR: does pressing B actually raise a floor on their machine? If not, ALSO chase an input bug (build_floor action = keycode 66 + physical_keycode 66, polled in tower_controller._process; robust two-event binding, should work). Key files: tower_controller.gd (_constructing/_update_constructing/_build_next_floor/_begin_exterior_walk), tower_hud.gd (set_construction/set_explore), scenes/garden/camera_modes_hud.gd (dead buttons), iso_camera.gd (bow-out).

queue.resolution: UNATTENDED overnight run (floor_population_spec OVERNIGHT SLICE). queue.title: Bind the world to a 24-hour clock (a day ~ 5 real minutes) — sunlight-driven shading
queue.detail: Operator intent surfaced during the opening-redesign playtest (2026-06-29): ultimately EVERYTHING should be bound to a running clock — a full 24-hour day/night cycle, simplest version a day runs over ~5 real minutes. The trigger was wanting the construction PIT to read as deeper via shading (one side darker than the other); operator's instinct is that this should be solved RELATIVE TO SUNLIGHT (a moving sun casting directional light + shadow into the pit), not hand-painted static shading — so pit depth-shading was DEFERRED to this work rather than faked now. Build on the existing TimeOfDay autoload (already drives a day/night clock that currently latches on at the GameDirector TEMPORAL phase; see D-003 item 3 + STATUS). Scope to decide when picked up: (a) a continuous wrapping clock (sim_time -> 0..1 day fraction) at ~5 min/day, decoupled from the linear arc; (b) a directional sun (DirectionalLight3D) whose pitch/azimuth + color/intensity track the clock (dawn/noon/dusk/night), giving real shadows that con+ read depth in the pit and on every floor; (c) ambient/sky tint per time-of-day. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED by the operator: 'hold off on the 24-hour cycle build... I want to keep moving through the 10-chunk [opening] arc before I engage time.' Pick this up AFTER the opening-sequence redesign (OR-001) chunks are done. Related: D-003 (time-of-day was listed as a TEMPORAL-phase concern), constants TOD_SUN_PITCH_*.
